description: Historical / baseline behavior prior to Phase C3 compilation, gate validation, modal safety, and simulation mock rigor contract hardening

stale_success_token.vulnerability: extract_clean_build_proof accepted bare counter string without any compilation activity, headers, or POU validation markers as a clean build.

zero_source_pous_compile.vulnerability: compile_project appended only a log warning and returned success=True when no Structured Text POUs were present in the project.

incomplete_gate_acceptance.vulnerability: assert_cscape_live accepted gate data marked ready_for_tests=True without verifying presence of valid positive PID and valid non-zero HWND.

compilation_empty_output.scenario: Output window scraping returns empty string
compilation_empty_output.vulnerability: Empty compilation output was treated as success because len(errors_list) == 0.

modal_auto_yes_and_foreign_handling.scenario: Modal #32770 dialog encountered during compilation pass

baseline_behavior.non_fatal_dialog: Auto-clicked IDYES (0x0111, 6) via PostMessageW to dismiss non-fatal error dialogs
baseline_behavior.foreign_modal: No PID filtering; unrecognized dialogs unhandled without fail-closed rejection

modal_auto_yes_and_foreign_handling.vulnerability: Blind auto-Yes masked non-fatal compilation faults; foreign modals could deadlock or cause unexpected UI states.

simulation_live_mode_and_taxonomy.scenario: Caller invokes simulation with mode='VERIFIED_LIVE' or ladder logic in POU

baseline_behavior.mode_verified_live: Did not check or prohibit mode='VERIFIED_LIVE' on pure-software simulation
baseline_behavior.ladder_logic_in_sim: Failed with generic exception (e.g. Unknown FB 'XIC') instead of fail-closed ERR_LADDER_FORBIDDEN
baseline_behavior.taxonomy_classification: Missing explicit CLASSIFICATION = 'TESTED_MOCK [offline/DEV only]' constants on simulator modules

simulation_live_mode_and_taxonomy.vulnerability: Simulation could ambiguously claim live status; ladder constructs in simulation leaked through ST boundary.
